title: How long?
author: cxdxix-
selftext:
How long should take your game development ? Is it something that you plan ? 

I feel that I always want to add features and I don’t know how much time a good game is supposed to take in terms of programmation?

comments.author: FluffyVegetable1476
comments.body:
I’m 3 weeks into my current. 

Everything is grey, the models are temporary and boxy but the functionality is absolutely sweet. 

Client and server running at 64tick. Jitter and loss protection working. Hit scan feeling smooth, projectiles performing as expected. 

Different map game modes are working well. 

Servers self-orchestrating on demand. 

Maybe, just maybe this week I will start on the first map being modelled out, then textured. 

Then build out a proper HUD.

replies.author: cxdxix-
replies.body: So you started with the server directly ? Multiplayer right ?

comments.author: FutureLynx_
comments.body: Prototype. 1 day - 1 month. Average game 1 month - 6 months. Good complex game like an rts 6 months - 2 years or more.

replies.author: LusikkaFeed
replies.body: Shit game 1-6 months. Average to good over a year.

comments.author: sevenoutdb
comments.body:
Day 16 for me on a vector based space shooter, core combat system feels pretty good, boss fights are coming along, now starting to fuss with progression/economy. I think this game can go from wondering if I can make a decent game with Claude to having a shippable game in 4 about 4 months. Plan everything once you have the initial game loop, be able to answer some basic questions like, "what does the player do" and "why do they do it". Later, answer questions like what is exciting about this game, who would play this game, and how much would they pay for this.

I used ChatGPT (Pro) to review gameplay footage, codebase and gave me fresh takes on the game, and came up with some valuable feedback and direction notes. 

Most importantly, MOVE FORWARD, start now, and show it to as many people as possible. Be able to compartmentalize feedback, and believe in yourself. Have a realistic goal, and that is smaking something that is fun to play. Then worry about the rest if you want to. Make game 80% of the time and play game 20% of the time. Switch to becoming a creator. Get organized, use github, build the game in a game engine if you can, then I think it will be easier to reuse techniques, tools, etc, and compound the lessons learned and solutions.

replies.body: Thanks ! It’s my first week, I’m prototyping but I already want to explain and show what I have

comments.author: Fringe_Walker_
comments.body:
I think ultimately depends on the tools that you're using. And the type of game you're trying to develop.

I personally am about twelve hours in and I got about eight more hours. I'm projecting before I have a solid demo of the full game that I intend on completing, and I'm thinking probably about a hundred hours total to complete or be release-able at least

comments.author: YKLKTMA
comments.body: Not sure what you consider a good game, but if you look at successful indie games, it’s usually 2-5 years of development by a team of 1-3 people. Not hard to calculate that solo it would take on average 5-10 years. Games like Hades/Hades2 are already 50-100 years.
